pair01.why: B's 'The work grows with the table, so a million rows means a million checks' and the closing 'Indexing every column slows writes without helping reads' are tidy, template-like; A's 'None of this is free' and 'So the habit to build is' are more conversational, and it adds the useful boolean-column planner caveat.

pair02.why: B leans on the stock 'phone book' analogy and 'open to the middle, throw away half, repeat'; A stays plain and covers the 'matches most of the table' case without a flourish.

pair03.why: A restates the facts twice (intro paragraph then a bold-labelled list) and pads with 'whether or not anything had changed'; B is compact and its review notes are a proposal, not a fact.

pair04.why: B's 'The speedup comes at a price, and writes pay it' and 'There is a planning cost too' are essay-style signposting; A is more direct with concrete 'eight indexes ... nine writes'.

pair05.why: A's 'At a thousand rows you will never notice. At fifty million you will.' is a staged rhetorical beat typical of model output; B is plainer and adds a concrete range-filter example.

pair06.why: A uses four headers ('Before', 'What changed', 'Why the cron job stays', 'Reviewing') for a tiny PR and repeats points; B is tighter and reviewer-oriented.

pair07.why: B is the stock 'Summary / Changes' bullet template; A reads as a short human PR description with 'so status changes are no longer tied to the polling interval'.

pair09.why: A has 'Both are slow and stressful, and both usually happen at the worst possible time' and 'in a few concrete ways', a stack of triads; B is tighter with the 'larger bet than it needs to be' point and a concrete proposal.
